built.summary:
I added the 3-axle 6x4 transit concrete mixer truck (name concrete_mixer_truck, abbrev CMT, category hauling). It passes its own check with 0 errors, and neither test suite has a failure for it.

I created only scripts/heavy_machines/machines/concrete_mixer_truck.py. The final run of `check_machine.py concrete_mixer_truck` printed OK and wrote assets/heavy_machines/concrete_mixer_truck/concrete_mixer_truck.urdf and .json. Renders are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vla-datagen/39bfe37a-c345-5663-b8fb-e785cd7a1b70/scratchpad/prev/concrete_mixer_truck/ (poses, sweeps, side, front and 3D close-ups, a drum rotation sequence, and rough pinhole views of the three cameras).

**What it looks like:** a white left-hand-drive cab-over cab sitting on the front axle, with windscreen, door and rear glass (visual only), a dark grille with bars, a steel bumper with headlights, a skid plate, mirrors, roof beacons, steps behind the front wheel and an air intake.
- **Chassis:** black frame rails, engine, radiator, front beam axle with track rod, two rear axle housings with differentials, tandem springs, fuel tank on the right, battery box and air tanks on the left, side guards, tandem fenders and mud flaps, rear underrun bar and tail lights.
- **Mixer:** water tank behind the cab, front pedestal with the drum gearbox and motor, and a grey stepped-cone drum tilted 12° with a roller track and two orange spiral stripes. A rear pedestal carries two rollers; above sit the charging hopper, a platform with a guard rail, and a ladder on the left. Under the opening are the collecting funnel, swivel ring and yoke, and the main chute with the extension folded on top and a visible lift cylinder.
- **Size and mass:** about 9.63 × 2.54 × 3.95 m in the travel pose against a 9.5 × 2.5 × 3.9 m envelope (+1.4%, +1.6%, +1.3%). Mass is 12,997 kg against 13,000 kg. All 10 wheels touch the ground (axle centres 0.538 m up) and everything else clears it.
- **Masses:** chassis 8,650 kg, drum 2,800 kg, ten wheels at 105 kg each, two front knuckles at 120 kg each, swivel 70 kg, chute 150 kg, lift cylinder 37 kg.

**Driving:** Ackermann front steer. Wheelbase 4.60 m from the front axle to the centre of the rear tandem (the fixed axle point is at x = 0, the tandem centre). Top speed 22 m/s, reverse 4 m/s, maximum virtual steer 0.60 rad (inner wheel 0.68 rad, outer 0.54 rad; steer joint limits ±0.80 rad). Steering rate is 0.17 rad/s, explained under "Remaining warnings". The rear tandem tyres use role 'wheel'. Turn = +1 turns left (checked in the tests).

**Tools (action order: drive, turn, drum, chute_swing, chute_lift):**
1. **drum:** continuous rotation about the tilted drum axis at up to 1.45 rad/s (13.9 rpm). +1 = "charge", −1 = "discharge". The stripes follow the internal mixing fins, so on +1 they travel toward the cab. I confirmed this numerically and in a step-by-step render.
2. **chute_swing:** swivel about a vertical pivot at the rear, ±1.55 rad (±89°), 0.30 rad/s, starts at 0 (pointing back). +1 = "ccw", −1 = "cw" (seen from above), and the checker verifies it. Because the chute points rearward, "ccw" moves its end toward the truck's right side.
3. **chute_lift:** −0.55 to +0.35 rad, 0.25 rad/s, +1 = "raise". It starts raised at +0.35 for travel. The lift cylinder is cosmetic and follows the chute within 1.2 cm across the whole range.

**Cameras:** front is the driver's eye (left seat), just ahead of the windscreen, pitched 0.25 rad down. Left and right sit on the mirror heads looking outward and forward (pitch 0.35, yaw ±0.70). All three are on the chassis link.

**Collisions:** no collision overlaps in the travel pose. I also checked the chute across its full swing and lift range and found none; its edge stays about 2 cm clear of the ladder at full left swing. I declared no allowed overlaps.
built.datasheet:
Model class: Volvo FMX 6x4 cab-over chassis (Mack Granite 6x4 is the same class) with a Liebherr HTM 905 / McNeilus 11 yd³ class rear-discharge drum.

Datasheet / listing numbers used:
- Chassis: wheelbase 3.90 m + 1.37 m tandem, so 4.60 m from the front axle to the tandem centre; front overhang 1.45 m.
- Tyres: 315/80 R22.5 all round (diameter 1.08 m, section 0.315 m), single front, dual rear.
- Track: front 2.05 m; rear dual centres 1.82 m with 0.35 m twin spacing, giving 2.49 m over the rear tyres.
- Day cab 2.30 m wide, roof 3.1 m above the ground.
- Drum: nominal 9 m³ (11.8 yd³), about 14 m³ geometric, maximum diameter 2.36 m, tilted 12°, 0–14 rpm.
- Hopper (loading) height 3.95 m.
- Chute: 180° swivel (±90°), main chute 1.5 m plus a folding extension.
- Empty mass about 13.0 t (chassis-cab about 9.0 t plus mixer about 4.0 t).
- Overall size 9.5 × 2.5 × 3.9 m.
- Top speed 80 km/h (governed), used as 22 m/s. Turning circle about 18 m (the model gives about 18.3 m).

Assumed / typical for the class:
- Drum shape: head cone 0.75 m long (diameter 1.6 to 2.36 m), straight section 1.10 m, rear cone 2.70 m (2.36 to 1.10 m), neck 0.25 m. Lowest point 1.24 m above the ground, opening centre 3.24 m, and the top line is nearly horizontal.
- Roller track diameter 1.34 m, 0.45 m ahead of the opening.
- Frame top 1.02 m, mixer subframe top 1.17 m above the ground.
- Chute swivel ring top 2.30 m above the ground and 1.95 m behind the tandem centre; chute hinge 0.30 m below the ring.
- Chute lift −31° to +20° by a hydraulic cylinder (stroke about 0.30 m, closed length 0.79 m).
- Hydraulic swivel 0.30 rad/s; chute lift 0.25 rad/s.
- Steering: inner wheel 39°, outer 31°; virtual steer rate 0.17 rad/s (about 3.5 s from centre to full lock).
- Reverse speed 4 m/s.
- Mass split as given in the summary.
- Drum turns clockwise seen from the rear when charging. The fins are a left-handed helix about the forward-pointing drum axis, so +1 moves the concrete toward the cab.
remaining_warnings: tool drum: directions 'charge'/'discharge' not auto-verifiable. Justified: the drum spins about its own axis, so the checker's raise/out/left tests cannot measure it, and no vocabulary word fits drum rotation. I verified the sign two ways: the near-side stripe pieces move toward +x (the cab) as the drum angle increases (x ≈ 1.02 → 1.17 → 1.33 m for q = −0.3, 0, +0.3), and a step-by-step side render (drum_sequence.png) shows the spirals moving toward the cab.

No camera sees a tool in the travel pose. The front camera looks forward at the road and the left/right mirror cameras look outward-forward, as the conventions require. The chute and hopper are at the rear and the drum is behind the mirrors, the same situation as rigid_haul_truck's dump body. Images will not show tool motion; covering that would need a rearward camera, which the front/left/right convention does not allow.

Steering rate is 0.17 rad/s rather than a brisker ~0.3–0.4 rad/s. This is plausible for a heavy truck (about 5 steering-wheel turns lock to lock, about 3.5 s from centre to full lock). With 0.40 rad/s and the 22 m/s top speed, test_turn_left_increases_yaw failed because the yaw wrapped past ±π, even though the truck turned left correctly (yaw reached about 4.9 rad by 3 s). See core_issues.
core_issues: test/test_env_logic.py::test_turn_left_increases_yaw checks the wrapped yaw (env._yaw is wrapped with atan2 each step) after 3 s at drive 0.7 and full turn. Any fast Ackermann machine whose yaw goes past π in that time fails even though it turns the right way. My first tuning (22 m/s, steer rate 0.40 rad/s) reached about 4.9 rad and failed; the yaw sampled every 0.5 s was 0.17, 0.69, 1.62, 2.76, −2.38, −1.23. I worked around it with steer_rate = 0.17, which ends at 2.69 rad. Suggested fix: add up the yaw rate (or unwrap the yaw) in the test, or use a shorter run or a lower drive command. backhoe_loader currently fails this same test at −1.53 rad, which may be the same cause.

checks.py's direction check defines 'left' as counter-clockwise seen from above, around the joint. For a part that points rearward (a mixer chute, a paver screed), counter-clockwise moves its end to the machine's RIGHT, so the words left/right mean the opposite of what a user would expect. I used 'ccw'/'cw' to stay accurate. A rear-aware rule or a recommended word pair would help keep the generated instructions consistent across machines.

The direction check samples a revolute joint only at its lower and upper limits. For a symmetric swing of about ±90° the two directions are nearly opposite, so the left/right test becomes ill-conditioned (≈0 at exactly ±π/2). I set the chute swing to ±1.55 rad instead of ±1.5708 to keep a measurable value. Comparing points near the start position (as the check already does for continuous joints) would avoid this.

The render.py 'front' view sorts depth so that it actually shows the machine from the REAR, with +y drawn on the right. This is not wrong for checks, but the panel title is misleading when judging the front of a machine; I used a separate true front view in my scratch tools.

issues.description: Turning behaviour at the 22 m/s road speed is unusable in this site environment. The shared scripted drivers command fixed fractions of max_speed, and 22 m/s is the highest top speed of the 18 machines (rigid_haul_truck 15, wheel_tractor_scraper 15.3). As a result, turn goals become long, physically impossible arcs, and the scripted demo leaves the prop field.
issues.evidence: I replayed the env's Ackermann model with TaskController (turn goals drive at 0.5, i.e. 11 m/s, with steer_rate 0.17). 'turn left 30 degrees' covers a 17.2 m path. 'turn left 90 degrees' covers a 29.7 m path (26.7 m displacement) with peak yaw rate 1.18 rad/s and lateral acceleration 13.0 m/s² (about 1.3 g; a mixer would roll over at about 0.35 g). Same 90° goal: rigid_haul_truck 19.5 m at 7.7 m/s², backhoe_loader 15 m. scripted_demo drives at 0.6 × 22 = 13.2 m/s for 3 s, about 40 m, which crosses the whole 14–34 m prop annulus.
issues.suggested_fix: Preferred: the core fix (see core_issues) that caps scripted turn speed or limits steer by lateral acceleration. Machine-side alternative: set Drive.max_speed to a site/yard speed (about 11 m/s, 40 km/h, as backhoe and crane use) and record the 80 km/h governed road speed in the docstring only.

issues.description: steer_rate = 0.17 rad/s was chosen to dodge a flawed test rather than for realism, and the docstring (lines 23-26) justifies a physical parameter by citing test_env_logic. A heavy truck turns its road wheels at about 0.3–0.4 rad/s when manoeuvring, so the truck reacts sluggishly to steering (3.5 s from centre to lock, 7 s lock to lock). That slowness also stretches turn arcs.
issues.evidence: With steer_rate 0.30, the 3 s test at drive 0.7 (15.4 m/s) builds up yaw = 15.4/4.6 × (−ln cos 0.6 / 0.3 + 1 × tan 0.6) ≈ 4.4 rad. That wraps past π, so the test fails even though the truck turns left correctly. The builder's 0.40 run reached 4.9 rad. backhoe_loader shows the same workaround (0.16).
issues.suggested_fix: First fix test_turn_left_increases_yaw so it unwraps the yaw (see core_issues). Then set steer_rate to about 0.30 and remove the test reference from the module docstring.

issues.description: None of the three cameras ever sees a tool (drum, chute_swing, chute_lift), so 3 of the 5 action channels leave no visual trace in VLA data.

issues.description: The machine's centre of mass is unrealistic: far forward and high. There is no effect in the kinematic env (gravity is disabled), but it would be wrong for anyone simulating dynamics from the URDF.

issues.description: Reference and docstring inconsistencies.

core_issues: test/test_env_logic.py::test_turn_left_increases_yaw asserts on env._yaw, which is wrapped with atan2 every step. Any fast Ackermann or articulated machine that yaws more than π in 3 s at drive 0.7 fails even though it turns the right way (confirmed: steer_rate 0.30 on this truck gives about 4.4 rad). This pushes builders to slow down steering artificially (concrete_mixer_truck 0.17, backhoe_loader 0.16). Fix: add up yaw_rate·dt (or unwrap the yaw) inside run() and assert on the total, or shorten the run or lower the drive command.

checks.py tool-direction check compares only the subtree centroid at j.lower and j.upper. For a symmetric revolute swing of ±θ, the cross product is proportional to sin(2θ): it is about 0 at ±π/2 (a spurious 'no measurable motion' warning) and NEGATIVE for θ > π/2. So a real 200° chute swivel or ±100° slew is falsely reported as 'moves the opposite way'. That forced this truck to ±1.55 rad. Fix: use init ± a small Δq for revolute joints too (as for continuous), or add up the cross products over small steps.

checks.py defines 'left' as counter-clockwise from above about the joint. For rear-pointing parts (mixer chute, backhoe swing, paver screed), 'left' therefore moves the part's end toward the machine's RIGHT, and machines now differ: backhoe_loader uses left/right, concrete_mixer_truck uses ccw/cw. Fix: document one convention, or verify 'left'/'right' by the sign of the tip's Δy in the root frame, and recommend one word pair for rear-pointing swings.

tasks.py instruction template f"{word} the {label} to {pct}%" produces ungrammatical text for direction words: 'ccw the chute swing to 90%', 'left the backhoe swing to 70%'. Fix: use a 'swing'/'move' verb for left/right/ccw/cw words, e.g. 'swing the chute ccw (left) to 90%'.

render.py _draw_ortho depth sorting is reversed for 'top' and 'front' (sgn = −1 draws the highest or front-most shapes first). The 'top' panel actually shows the machine from BELOW: the mixer's engine is drawn over the cab roof and the tandem tyres over the fenders. The 'front' panel shows it from the REAR. Fix: use sgn = +1.0 for 'top' and 'front'.

tasks.TaskController (turn goals at drive 0.5, at least 0.25 for drive goals) and scripted_demo (0.6 for 3 s) use fixed fractions of max_speed, and machine_env has no speed-dependent steering or lateral-acceleration limit. For road-speed machines this gives turns at about 1.3 g with 30 m arcs (mixer: 13 m/s² on a 90° turn) and 40 m demo runs straight through the 14–34 m prop annulus. Fix: cap the scripted speed (e.g. v_turn ≤ about 4 m/s, v_drive ≤ about 5 m/s), and/or clamp |steer| to atan(a_lat_max·L/v²) in _apply_action.

The camera convention (front, plus left/right looking outward-forward) cannot show tools at the rear: the mixer drum and chute, the rigid haul truck body, the paver screed. Their tool channels have no visual evidence in the VLA data. Consider an optional 4th 'rear'/'tool' camera, or allow left/right to face rearward for machines whose tools sit behind the cab.

urdf_builder.link_inertia spreads a link's mass over its shapes by volume, so hollow boxes such as cabs and tanks dominate the centre of mass and inertia (mixer: front axle 67% against about 45% real). Harmless while gravity is disabled, but wrong for any dynamic use of the URDFs. Consider an optional per-shape mass or density, or an explicit link centre of mass.

Two deliberate departures from the brief:
1. **Steering is on the counterweight-end axle, not the platform end.** JLG's drive-orientation article says the normal driving position has the boom over the rear drive (non-steer) wheels, and Genie's drive-enable logic says the same about the non-steer tyres. So the steered axle sits under the counterweight. I kept +x = platform end, which is the direction the operator faces and the natural travel direction. That makes the model steer_axle = "rear", like a forklift, with fixed_axle_x set to the platform-end axle. If you want the brief's literal "front steer", the platform has to face −x and the operator camera would look into the boom.
2. **The boom has three sections, not two.** Two sections cannot reach 18 m from a stowed boom of about 6.2 m, so the 60 ft class uses a base plus two telescoping sections. I modelled the second telescoping section as a follower, so it is still one telescope tool.

core_issues: test_env_logic.test_tools_respect_limits_and_wrap drives every tool for a fixed 30*15 control steps (15 s) and requires it to reach both limits. Slow, safety-limited machines such as aerial work platforms and cranes therefore cannot use realistic function speeds. Suggested fix: scale the step count per tool by (upper - lower) / velocity.

render.py _draw_ortho uses depth = sgn*mean for painter ordering. For 'top' (sgn=-1 on z) the highest shapes are drawn first and lower ones over them, so the 'top' panel shows the machine from below (tyres drawn over the turntable, platform floor over its rails). The 'front' panel (sgn=-1 on x) shows the rear: the counterweight face and tail lights end up on top. Flipping sgn for top and front (and +1 to -1 for side if the left-side view is wanted) fixes it. It is cosmetic only and I worked around it with a local renderer.

TaskController has a 40 s per-goal timeout and samples continuous-tool goals up to 180°, so any continuous tool needs at least about 0.085 rad/s. This is fine here at 0.10 rad/s, but it caps how realistic slow slewing machines can be.

These failures belong to other agents' in-progress files, not this machine: backhoe_loader fails validation (box interpenetrations) and test_turn_left_increases_yaw. backhoe_loader and rough_terrain_crane also have no generated assets yet.

issues.description: The counterweight's 'lower lip behind the tyres' cuts through the wheels whenever the turntable slews. Slewing is the most common tool, and a real counterweight is designed to clear the tyre tops when it swings (that is what tailswing describes).
issues.evidence: The lip is box(0.58, 1.90, 0.20) at turntable z = -0.15, so its bottom is 1.12 - 0.25 = 0.87 m above the ground, while the tyre tops are at 1.04 m. I swept slew in 3° steps and sampled the tyre surfaces. Tyre points end up 0.10 m deep inside the lip at slew of about 15° (rear_right_wheel), 135° (front_right), 195-216° (front_left) and 300° (rear_left), with or without steer. The OBB check reports 0.17 m. The main counterweight block bottom is 1.07 m above the ground, so only the lip is at fault. checks.py tests only the init pose (slew 0), where the lip sits 7 cm behind the tyre, which is why it passed.
issues.suggested_fix: Delete the lip shape `box(0.58, 1.90, 0.20, at=(-2.11, 0.0, -0.15), ...)` in _counterweight(). Alternatively raise its bottom to at least 1.07 m above the ground (turntable z ≥ -0.05). Tailswing (rear face at TAIL_R) does not change.

issues.description: Every boom raise from the stowed pose drives the boom tail into the counterweight. The base section runs 0.30 m behind the foot pin and has a solid tail block. At q = 0 its bottom sits only 2 cm above the counterweight top, so raising the boom swings the tail down into the block.
issues.evidence: FK with OBB box-box penetration between boom_base and counterweight: 0.005 at 5°, 0.027 at 10°, 0.047 at 15°, 0.064 at 20°, 0.078 at 25°, 0.075 at 30°, 0.050 at 40°, 0.031 at 45°, clear from 55°. The counterweight main block spans turntable x -2.20 to -1.50 with its top at z = 0.80; the pivot is at (-1.45, 1.13). Under checks.py's own rule (box-box > OVERLAP_TOL 0.03) this would be an ERROR if it happened in the init pose.
issues.suggested_fix: Set BASE_X0 = -0.10 and the tail block shrinks with it. I verified on a patched build that boom_base vs counterweight penetration is 0 at every boom angle from 0 to 75° in 1° steps. Alternatively move the counterweight block's front face to x ≤ -1.65 or lower its top locally.

issues.description: At high boom angles the jib's lower arm clips through the fly head. The jib angle is referenced to horizontal through the levelling bracket, but the jib pivot is only 0.30 m ahead of the tip pin. The 0.26 × 0.42 × 0.52 fly head rotates with the boom and reaches that pivot. The task sampler picks boom and jib targets independently, and the jib starts at -65°, so 'raise the boom' followed by a small jib change reaches these poses routinely.
issues.evidence: OBB penetration of the boom_fly head (shape 1) against the jib lower-arm beam (shape 1): 0.05 m at boom 45° / jib -65°, 0.108 at 60°/-65°, 0.12 at 75°/-65°, 0.062 at 75°/-40°. At boom 75° the jib must be at -15° or higher to clear. The init pose is fine, which is why checks.py passed.
issues.suggested_fix: Set JIB_PIVOT = (0.45, 0.0). On a patched build, the worst fly/jib penetration across boom 0-75° × jib -65..+70° × telescope 0 is 0, validate() passes with no warnings, and the stowed length becomes 9.76 m (3% over the envelope). Extend the jib_base bracket box so it reaches the pivot pins (see the nit below).

issues.description: The platform-rotation DOF is missing. Every telescopic boom in this class has a platform rotator: Genie S-60 X/XC 160°, JLG 600S/600SJ 180°. The model has a rotator cylinder but it is only visual, so the operator cannot yaw the basket. That is a standard positioning function and the user wants broad machine coverage.
issues.evidence: _platform() draws `cyl(0.13, 0.62, ...)  # rotator`, but no joint yaws the basket. tools = slew/boom/telescope/jib only. Spec listings for the S-60 X/XC give 160° platform rotation.
issues.suggested_fix:
1. Split out a 'rotator' link (rotator cylinder plus mounting arm) as the child of platform_level_joint.
2. Add Joint('platform_rotate_joint', 'revolute', 'rotator', 'platform', xyz=(0.05, 0, 0), axis=(0, 0, 1), lower=-1.40, upper=1.40, velocity=0.25, role='tool').
3. Add Tool('platform_rotate_joint', 'platform_rotate', positive='left', negative='right'). The basket centroid is about 0.8 m off the axis, so checks.py can auto-verify the label.
4. Keep the front camera on 'platform' so it turns with the basket, as the operator does.

This gives 5 tools, within the 8 teleop key pairs.

issues.description: The boom, telescope and jib speeds are 3-4x the real ANSI-limited function speeds, so the platform moves at unrealistic speeds at height. The builder documents that this is forced by the shared 15 s test horizon.
issues.evidence: Boom 0.11 rad/s at about 16.7 m radius moves the platform at about 1.8 m/s. Telescope 0.36 m/s per section gives 0.72 m/s at the tip. Real S-60 X class: boom up 75° takes about 40-55 s (≈0.025-0.03 rad/s), extend about 35-45 s. test_env_logic.test_tools_respect_limits_and_wrap runs a fixed 30*15 steps.
issues.suggested_fix: Once the shared test scales its horizon by (upper - lower) / velocity (see core_issues), set boom ≈ 0.03 rad/s, telescope ≈ 0.12 m/s per section and jib ≈ 0.09 rad/s, and remove the 3x caveat from the docstring and notes.

issues.description: The levelling-bracket link jib_base is a solid 0.24 × 0.40 × 0.56 box that stays level while the fly head rotates, so it pokes visibly through the head and the fly body. checks.py does not catch this because the links are adjacent. The bracket also ends at x = 0.20 while the jib pin bosses span x 0.23-0.37, so the jib appears to float 3 cm from its bracket.
issues.evidence: OBB penetration of jib_base against the boom_fly head: 0.10 m at boom 0°, 0.23 at 30°, 0.33 at 75°, plus 0.14 into the fly body at 75°. The bracket box spans x -0.04 to 0.20 and the pins are at x 0.30 with radius 0.07.
issues.suggested_fix: Model the bracket as two clevis side plates outside the head: about box(0.42, 0.03, 0.56) at y = ±0.245, spanning x from -0.05 to the jib pivot plus 0.07. Or at least extend the box to the pivot and keep it within the head's ±0.21 m width.

issues.description: The mass distribution and the unrestricted reach make the model statically unstable at full horizontal outreach, where the real machine is stable with margin. There is no runtime effect today because gravity is disabled and the base is kinematic. It matters if dynamics are ever enabled, and it is a realism inconsistency.
issues.evidence: Boom at 0°, full extension, jib at 0°, slewed 90°: whole-machine CoM at y = 0.94 m unloaded and 1.28 m with a 230 kg basket load. The tyre centreline is at 1.015 m and the outer edge at 1.245 m, so the CoM is outside the support polygon. Reach is 17.28 m against 15.4-15.5 m on the datasheet (+12%). Shifting 700 kg from the chassis and turntable to the counterweight only brings the loaded CoM to 1.15 m. Cutting the stroke to 3.65 m gives 15.41 m reach and 1.04 m, but the platform height drops to 16.6 m.
issues.suggested_fix: At minimum, state in the docstring that the unrestricted reach envelope is statically unstable and give these figures. For better realism, move upper-structure mass rearward: counterweight about 3.6 t, engine and hydraulic trays centred behind the slew axis, chassis and turntable lighter to keep the total. Note that the datasheet reach comes from an extension-limited envelope near horizontal that this joint model cannot express.

issues.description: The datasheet attribution looks mislabelled. 22,930 lb (10.4 t) appears to be the Genie S-60 X figure. The S-60 XC (Xtra Capacity, 454 kg) carries a larger counterweight and is heavier.
issues.evidence: The docstring says 'operating mass 10.4 t (S-60 XC 22 930 lb ...)'. Spec listings give the S-60 XC tailswing as 1.41 m against 1.22 m for the S-60 X, which points to the larger counterweight. The model's 1.22 m tailswing matches the S-60 X / 600S.
issues.suggested_fix: Relabel the 10.4 t / 2.49 m / 1.22 m tailswing figures as Genie S-60 X (or JLG 600S/600SJ) and drop 'XC' from the reference.

core_issues: checks.py checks self-overlap and ground clearance only in the init pose. Here it missed three box-box interpenetrations above OVERLAP_TOL in ordinary reachable poses: counterweight lip vs tyres while slewing (0.10-0.17 m), boom tail vs counterweight while raising (0.078 m), and jib vs fly head at high boom angles (0.12 m). Suggested fix: also sweep each tool across its range with the others at init, slew a continuous tool in about 15° steps, and test the pairwise extremes of consecutive arm joints. Report as warnings at first.

test_env_logic.test_tools_respect_limits_and_wrap drives every tool for a fixed 30*15 control steps, so every tool must cover its range in 15 s. That forces aerial work platforms, cranes and telehandlers to 3-4x their real function speeds. Suggested fix: scale the step count per tool by ceil((upper - lower) / velocity) + margin.

Drive has no reduced speed when elevated. Aerial work platforms cut drive to about 0.3 m/s once the boom is raised or extended (Genie S-60 X: 0.68 mph raised). The env lets the TBL drive at 1.7 m/s with the platform at 18 m. Telehandlers and cranes have similar interlocks. Suggested fix: add an optional Drive.elevated_speed plus a stowed predicate (for example a list of (joint, max_q) thresholds) and clamp v in machine_env._apply_action.

render.py _draw_ortho has its painter's order inverted. For 'top' (sgn = -1 on z) and 'front' (sgn = -1 on x), far shapes are drawn last, over near ones. The side view is plotted as seen from -y (+x to the right) but sorts +y last, so it has the same inversion. Cosmetic only.
TaskController's 40 s per-goal timeout combined with continuous-tool goals of up to 180° requires at least about 0.085 rad/s on any slewing tool. That caps how realistic slow slew rates can be.

Latent: test_reset_and_cameras asserts every camera is within 15 m (xy) of the root. A long-reach machine's platform camera is about 16.7 m from the root at full horizontal extension (TBL). The test passes today only because it runs 20 steps.

applied: must_fix 1 (counterweight lip cuts through the tyres while slewing): confirmed. My slew × steer sweep reproduced 0.17 m OBB penetration, all from the lip shape, at slew 15/129/198/294°. Deleted the lip box(0.58, 1.90, 0.20) from _counterweight(). The remaining underside is 1.07 m above the ground, above the 1.04 m tyre tops, and the sweep now shows no penetration at any slew/steer angle. Tailswing is unchanged.

must_fix 2 (boom tail runs into the counterweight while raising): confirmed. Penetration was 0.005/0.027/0.047/0.064/0.078/0.075/0.050/0.031 m at 5/10/15/20/25/30/40/45°, peaking at 0.085 m at 28°. Set BASE_X0 = -0.10. I also shortened the tail block from 0.30 to 0.20 m (now x -0.10..0.10), because a 0.30 m block would have overlapped the retracted mid section, which starts at x = 0.13. boom_base vs counterweight is now clear at every angle from 0 to 75° in 1° steps, and boom_base vs turntable stays clear.

must_fix 3 (fly head clips the jib's lower arm): confirmed. I measured 0.050/0.108/0.120/0.062 m at the poses the reviewer gave. Set JIB_PIVOT = (0.45, 0.0). fly vs jib is now clear over boom 0-75° × jib -65..+70° × telescope 0/full × rotation ±80°.

should_fix 4 (add the platform-rotation DOF): applied. New 'rotator' link (actuator housing, visual clevis plates and cap) is the child of platform_level_joint. New platform_rotate_joint is revolute about z from rotator to platform, ±80° (160°, the Genie S-60 X/XC figure, confirmed by spec sheets), 0.25 rad/s, role tool. Added Tool('platform_rotate_joint', 'platform_rotate', positive='left', negative='right'); checks.py auto-verifies the 'left' label. The front camera stays on 'platform', so it turns with the basket. Masses: platform 190 kg + rotator 70 kg = the old 260 kg, total 10 420 kg. This gives 5 tools.

Follow-up to 4 (not in the review): splitting the platform from the jib exposed an existing hidden intersection. At jib +70° with the basket rotated ±80°, the jib's lower arm went 0.13 m into the basket mount, and at all rotations through the rotator housing. checks.py never saw it because jib and platform used to be adjacent links. Cause: in the rigid parallelogram model the jib-arm ends sweep about 0.17 m around the tip pin. Fix: rotator axis moved from 0.05 to ROT_X = 0.32 m ahead of the tip pin, clevis plates (y ±0.11, outside the jib arms) bridge the gap, the basket keeps a 0.20 m gap ahead of the axis (PLAT_X0 = ROT_X + 0.20), and the mount weldment stays within r ≈ 0.18 m of the axis behind it. A sweep of platform/rotator/jib/jib_base against every non-adjacent link over boom 0-75 × telescope 0/full × jib -65..+70 × rotation {-80, -40, 0, 40, 80} found no positive penetration. Adjacent pairs (jib–rotator, jib_base–fly) are also clear.

nit 6 (levelling bracket box pokes through the fly head): confirmed. I measured 0.10/0.23/0.33 m at boom 0/30/75°. Replaced the solid box with two clevis plates box(0.57, 0.03, 0.56) at y = ±0.245, outside the fly head's ±0.21, running from x -0.05 to JIB_PIVOT + 0.07 = 0.52. Lengthened the jib pins to 0.52 m and the tip pin to fw + 0.18 so both go through the plates. jib_base vs fly is now clear at every boom angle.

nit 7 (statically unstable at full outreach): numbers confirmed (CoM y 0.935 m unloaded, 1.278 m with a 230 kg load, original model; 0.96/1.31 m now). Applied the minimum fix: a 'Stability' paragraph in the docstring with these figures, the 1.015 m tyre centreline and 1.245 m outer edge, the reason (no extension-limited envelope, mass too far forward) and the note that it has no runtime effect. Also a line in notes. I did not move mass: the reviewer's own 700 kg shift only brings the loaded CoM to 1.18 m (I checked), so it does not fix stability and would be a guess without a real counterweight figure.

Docstring 'Model check' figures refreshed from offline FK: platform floor 18.42 m (unchanged), unrestricted outreach 17.7 m (was 17.3), stowed 9.93 × 2.53 × 2.59 m (was 9.61). Added a line on the interference sweeps, the new assumed geometry (0.10 m boom tail, 0.45 m jib pivot, 0.32 m rotator axis, counterweight underside 1.07 m) and the rotator rate. Description now mentions the 160° rotator.

I looked at the poses and sweeps PNGs plus my own close-ups of the jib tip at boom 0/75 × jib -65/+70, rotated ±80°, and the boom root at 25°; all look correct. test_machines.py: 18 tests OK. test_env_logic.py: 9 tests OK, including tool limits within 15 s and the task controller with the new platform_rotate tool. rejected.reason: Deferred, not wrong. The reviewer makes it conditional on the shared test scaling its horizon, and that has not happened. test_env_logic.test_tools_respect_limits_and_wrap still runs a fixed 30*15 steps (15 s), and tasks.TaskController still has a 40 s timeout per goal. At 0.03 rad/s the boom needs 43.6 s for its 1.31 rad range, so both tests would fail. I may only edit this machine file, so I kept the current rates and the 3x caveat in the docstring and notes. rejected.issue: nit 8: relabel the 10.4 t / 22,930 lb figure as Genie S-60 X and drop 'XC'
rejected.reason: The relabel is wrong. Published specs give the S-60 X 4WD as 20,740 lb / 9,408 kg (2WD 20,570 lb), so 10.4 t is not the S-60 X. 22,930 lb / 10,401 kg is listed for the S-60 XC (aerialequipmentparts.com/pages/machine-specs/genie-s60xc), while Genie's own sheet gives the XC 21,967 lb / 9,964 kg (macallisterrentals.com/files/S-60_65-Spec-Sheet.pdf; aerialequipmentparts.com/pages/machine-specs/genie-s60x). The reviewer is right that the XC is heavier and that some listings give it a 1.41 m tailswing, so I clarified the docstring instead of relabelling: 10.4 t = S-60 XC 4WD in dealer listings (Genie sheet 9.96 t), S-60 X 4WD 9.4 t, 1.22 m tailswing = Genie S-60 X sheet (some XC listings 1.41 m). Model mass and tailswing unchanged.

remaining_warnings: validate() reports no errors and no warnings.

Stowed length is 9.93 m against the 9.45 m envelope (+5%, under the 10% warning threshold). It grew by 0.32 m from the reviewer's jib-pivot move (+0.15) and the rotator-axis move (+0.17) that keeps the rotated basket clear of the jib.

Unrestricted horizontal outreach is 17.7 m against the 15.4 m datasheet (+15%), and that pose is statically unstable (CoM 0.96 m unloaded, 1.31 m loaded, tyre centreline 1.015 m). It is documented and has no runtime effect because gravity is disabled and the base is kinematic. A real fix needs coupled extension/angle limits, which the joint model cannot express.
Boom, telescope and jib rates are still about 3x real speeds until the shared tests scale their horizon (should_fix 5, deferred).
